findings.finding: F1: Design §6 names a production checker command but also says HUMAN_ONLY means 'no agent can observe a live session’s header'. A5 nevertheless requires actual header evidence from a session carrying the new pi-envoy. The draft flags the conflict but leaves that required deliverable without an executable observation path.
findings.answer: Architect decided (Envoy reply 2026-10-25T16:03Z; issue comment 6adc9908-1cae-4039-92fa-ed1ada81a00e): the production record is dispatch-production-check.sh output for /agents/<id>/live with --route /api/v1/agents/<id>/stream and /messages, plus proof a live session runs a pi-envoy carrying the change (legion version plugins line in a pod started after the image deploy). No live header, no person asked, nothing switched. Recorded in specDepartures.

findings.finding: F2: A2 says 'After a person picks a model there, the session’s next turn runs on it'. The design disables only the pickers while pending. A pick is not an atomic model change, and the existing delivery path does not serialize a following prompt behind completion of that change.
findings.answer: Decision 9: 'next turn' means the next turn after the session answers the switch; the reply is posted only after the built-in's handle (setModel) finishes. Decision 8 disables the composer's Send while a switch is pending so the page's own next prompt follows the answer. A running turn finishes on its model; other people's or the terminal's prompts are outside the page and documented. Rig check 8 (picker-during-turn) and browser row 4 prove it.

findings.finding: F3: The rule 'responding === true, a replay has arrived, and no settings frame came' is not evidence of an older pi-envoy. The draft itself withholds settings on a current build when AgentRegistry cannot find the session. Separately, settings plus command names is only advertised capability, not proof that typed input can execute.
findings.answer: Decision 7 table: responding=false shows no notice; no replay yet shows no notice; replay without settings frame = older pi-envoy notice; current pi-envoy that cannot read the session publishes reported:false with its own notice; reported settings without model/effort commands = terminal-only notice and no picker. A commands listing is treated as an offer; a refusal comes back as the session's reply. Browser rows 2-3 and rig check 17 cover them.

findings.finding: F4: The proposed 30-second no-answer deadline is not aligned with a cancellation or execution deadline. A still-fresh human attempt can execute after the page times out. In addition, 'failed at send' is not necessarily an HTTP failure, and the planned stopped-session local step does not necessarily exercise A4.
findings.answer: Decision 8: clock starts when the POST answers; a 201 whose attempt is failed ends at once with the attempt error; the 30 s no-answer text says only that no answer came, never 'not applied'; a late reply to the latest switch replaces it; an earlier switch's reply never touches a newer status. Rig check 13 uses SIGSTOP after a successful send, SIGCONT past the one-minute accept window, and asserts ACCEPT_STALE and unchanged host settings.

findings.finding: F5: The proposed real-stack run lacks a grounded model/provider fixture for successful model switching and fallback, and its refusal injects a settings list that the real session never reported. That injection can test an adversarial selection, but cannot substitute for A2's genuine available-model contract.
findings.answer: Task 6: models come from the caller's own provider keys (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY in the pod), two defaults chosen from get_available_models and preflighted; fallback via a rig-broken provider plus retry.fallbackChains; the refusal check publishes an injected settings list (labelled injected in the README) and the real session answers 'No API key'; genuine lists are compared with RPC get_available_models and /effort independently of the page.

findings.finding: F6: The named proof scenarios do not yet decide several clauses of A1/A2. Naming 'model + effort switch', resume, and defaults is not enough to establish the exact configured-thinking behavior and audit/isolation requirements.
findings.answer: Task 6 checks map each A2 clause: picker options vs host lists (1), message route (3), next turn model (4), auto kept (5), level after model pick vs a twin session's /model (6), effort (7), refusal (9), other session unchanged (12), resume (14), new-session defaults (15), attribution by a second person (18); browser rows 4-7.

findings.finding: F7: A5's before/after browser runs have no reproducible mechanics, and the claimed WebKit-phone run will not select the proposed new file under the current configuration.
findings.answer: Task 5 names the baseline as fork_point(main@origin | @-), a self-contained test file restored onto it with jj restore, the exact bun run e2e command for chromium and iphone at head and baseline, expected results (all rows fail at baseline except the A3 regression guard), the webkit-iphone selector and grep update, CI carrying webkit-iphone because a pod cannot start it, and no concurrent rig run.

findings.finding: F8: The local timing proof needs a browser that stays open across changes, not two snapshots obtained by reopening the page. Also, typing '/model <id>' into this fork's TUI does not execute the same text handler used by sendUserInput: its TUI handler opens the selector.
findings.answer: Task 6's driver holds one Chromium page open for every check; Oh My Pi runs in --mode rpc (as Legion panes do), and the host's own routes are RPC set_model, set_thinking_level and a typed /effort prompt, timed from the RPC answer to the header change. Fallback is read as 'header follows the fallback within 20 s with no further user turn' (check 16).

findings.finding: F9: Publishing settings before posting the reply does not order what the browser observes. Settings frames and message.answered/refetch travel independently. The draft does not specify which state wins when replies, HTTP completion, frames, replay, and timeout cross.
findings.answer: Decision 8: the header shows only the latest settings frame by seq; the switch outcome is the reply to that message id, independent of frame order; refusals produce no frame and the header keeps its values; a reply already present when the POST returns ends the switch. Unit tests in use-session-switch.test.ts and browser row 10 cover the crossings.

findings.finding: F10: The draft caps the model list at 500 and each identifier at 200 characters while A2 promises every available model. It also promises that settings always ride in replay without explaining how their budget combines with the already-prioritized commands frame.
findings.answer: Decisions 1 and 3: the model list is never cut and ids are never truncated (display only); settings paid first, then commands, then history; commands stay last. A 5,000-model test pins the budget; the bound past max_payload is the existing logged replay failure.

findings.finding: F11: The real forged-switch negative needs a settings oracle. The existing user-turn rig's usual 'no user message was injected' check cannot prove that /model or /effort did not execute: successful built-ins themselves submit no user message.
findings.answer: Rig check 10: a forged person-shaped steer on the session's agent subject naming a non-existent attempt with body /model <B>, plus an Envoy message /effort high from a second client; the session file shows each as a card; RPC get_state and /effort are unchanged before and after. The accept path is unchanged.

findings.finding: F12: The draft names no documentation or changelog work, although the feature changes the published live-view behavior, plugin wire protocol, host requirements, and live-proof procedure.
findings.answer: Tasks 3, 4, 6, 7 list the docs: pi-envoy AGENTS.md and CHANGELOG.md, contracts CHANGELOG.md, envoy CHANGELOG.md (the SPA ships with Dispatch), packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md, docs/site agents.md live view section, scripts/e2e/README.md (index row and a section on how the rig differs from dispatch-user-turns.sh).

findings.finding: G2-1: The clock-skew risk did not state the ordering guarantee the seq seed gives, and the contract promises unconditional cross-process monotonicity.
findings.answer: Decision 3a states the condition 1000*(t1-t0) > N, accepts the limit (persisting the counter would add a write per frame), has the contract's seq doc name that basis, and cites the injected-clock test agent-stream.test.ts:579-623 as the deterministic check. 'Every frame' corrected to every settings and commands frame.

findings.finding: G2-2: Row 11d left unresolved whether a held step survives a reported value that changes that picker.
findings.answer: Amended decision 8: a held step survives the switch's end unless the session reports a new value for that picker, which drops it (SessionSettings.tsx:95-97,114,126; unit tests AgentConversationPage.test.tsx:898-904 and 1038-1079). Row 11d names its values: model switch a->b, thinking stays auto, Enter then sends /effort for the step.

findings.finding: G2-3: Rig check 14 did not isolate publishState on a real surface and its evidence followed a reload.
findings.answer: Check 14 has three steps on one held-open page: the switch stays; numbering (RPC set_thinking_level after a first-watch barrier); arming (relaunch with --resume --model <other>, page follows with no RPC change). Screenshot before any reload. Negative control: a throwaway rig run with publishState removed fails step 3 only; the tester's red run is cited for numbering.

findings.finding: G2-4: selectOption does not drive a native popup; the arrow-key claim ignored macOS.
findings.answer: Decision 6a labels the path accurately: selectOption fires change outside a key's task, which is what a pointer or native-popup pick delivers; Playwright cannot drive a native popup; macOS arrows open the popup and step nothing (AgentMessageComposer.tsx:118-126). Same as the issue picker's own spec.

findings.finding: G2-5: Task 8 asked the implementer to record CI results for a head not yet pushed.
findings.answer: The implementer records --list for webkit and firefox and does not wait; the tester reads CI on the pushed head and records the webkit and firefox results by run id.

findings.finding: G2-6: The simplify instruction asked for a second pass and its range excluded 9f93e30b.
findings.answer: Dropped: the simplify pass runs once per pull request and ran at 5ac927eb -> 04c4a43b (pr-body.md).

specDepartures.spec: A5: after the deploy, the production check is recorded with the header of one live session started on a build carrying this pi-envoy showing its model and thinking level.
specDepartures.plan: The production record is dispatch-production-check.sh output for /agents/<id>/live with --route /api/v1/agents/<id>/stream and --route /api/v1/agents/<id>/messages, plus proof a live session runs a pi-envoy carrying the change (legion version plugins line in a pod started after the worker image deploy). No live header is recorded and nothing is switched.
specDepartures.evidence: The live view's data is person-only: an agent bearer gets 403 HUMAN_ONLY (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/routes_table.go:110-112, server.go:731-743). The deployment instructions say the check reaches only the build and page for such pages, the browser test proves person-only data, and no person is asked to look. The architect accepted this reading on 2026-10-25 (Envoy reply; issue comment 6adc9908-1cae-4039-92fa-ed1ada81a00e) and keeps the spec unchanged.
